summary: US-016: Group and agency long-lived reservations
description:
### US-016: Group and agency long-lived reservations
**As** an organizer, **I want** to grant a group or agency a long-lived reservation they draw down
over time, so bulk buyers don't fight the public TTL. **Priority:** P2 **Depends on:** US-014
(typed-claim machinery; soft)
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] A reservation claim type with an explicit expiry date (not the cart TTL), placeable by
      staff for a named counterparty; counts against capacity like any claim (and against a
      channel allocation when one applies).
- [ ] Draw-down: quantity converts to confirmed orders **partially and repeatedly** (10 of 200
      today, 50 next week) without the unconverted remainder ever passing through a publicly
      claimable state; unconverted quantity returns to sale at expiry (lazy, DB-time).
- [ ] The order/payment side of a draw-down uses the existing commerce checkout seam; agency
      pay-later terms, invoicing and dunning are explicitly TKT-34 (non-goal).
- [ ] Contention test covers concurrent public holds racing a reservation draw-down.

**Quality gates (every story):**
- `make check` green (lint + unit + integration + smoke; mirrors CI)
- Contract tests pass for any touched service boundary (ADR-009 drift check)
- Money/ticket-path: audit-trail invariants hold (ADR-003)
- Read-endpoint changes: ADR-004 TTL tier declared with rationale

Parent epic: TKT-4. Full lineage: docs/product/prd-v1.md §TKT-4.

objective.note: Epic COS 4 (group/agency): long-lived reservations drawn down over time without fighting the cart TTL.

scope.note: IN: reservation claim type with explicit expiry + counterparty, repeated partial conversion to confirmed orders, lazy expiry give-back, race test vs public holds. OUT: pay-later terms, invoicing, dunning (TKT-34).

uncertainties.note: Partial-quantity claim mechanics (split rows vs decrement) settled in Planning — same fork as US-014's partial convert; reuse its answer.

dependencies.note: Soft on US-014 (typed-claim machinery) — not wired as a blocker; Planning reuses its type/partial mechanics if landed.

approach.note: Reservation type + counterparty + explicit expires_at; draw-down converts quantity to the commerce checkout flow atomically; expiry reuses the lazy sweep.

first_slice.note: Reserve 200 for an agency, convert 10 to a confirmed order, let the rest expire → 190 return to sale, never publicly claimable mid-conversion.

binding.rule: The inventory database is the sole write-side correctness boundary. Each mutation locks the inventory pool row first, then its claim rows; operations addressed by hold ID discover the pool with a non-locking read, then re-read the claim after locking the pool — every path has the same pool-to-claim lock order. A claim is held, confirmed, released, or expired; the last three are terminal. PostgreSQL time decides expiry: a transaction expires due holds before capacity accounting, so cleanup jobs are optional optimizations. Confirmed plus unexpired-held quantity may never exceed pool capacity. Hold creation requires an organizer-scoped idempotency key, single-use across the claim's full lifecycle. Reserved seats, date ranges, and entitlements reuse the lifecycle and lock ordering but add their own resource constraints.

governingAdrs.why: A group reservation is a claim with an explicit expiry — draw-down must keep the pool→claim lock order and never round-trip capacity through public availability.
Draw-down rides the existing commerce checkout seam — contract changes on both sides are drift-checked.
